paragraphs: Rav Shmuel bar Abba of Hagronia.

[Bava Kamma 88a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.88a.21) relates that his mother married Rabbi Abba. She assigned her property to her son Rav Shmuel (whom Hyman identifies as her son from her first husband, Rabbi Abba of Hagronia) and died. [Rav Shmuel went to Rav Yirmeyah bar Abba](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.88b.1-2), who established his right to the property. Rabbi Abba reported the matter to Rav Hoshaya, who reported it to Rav Yehudah; he ruled that the property belonged to Rabbi Abba.[^2]
He also asked Rabbi Abba a question in Bava Kamma 6b.[^1]

notes.text: The property case continues at 88b. Hyman distinguishes Rav Shmuel’s father from the later husband, also called Abba. The question Hyman cites as 6b is at [Bava Kamma 7b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.7b.14-17), which calls the questioner Rav Shmuel bar Abba of Akroneya. Hyman treats it as an attestation of the man from Hagronia.
Bava Kamma calls Yirmeyah Rabbi where Hyman has Rav. In the continuation, Rav Yehudah answers by citing Shmuel’s ruling.
